record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.context_brief: Classification with a sub pseudo-oval present
record.original_question: Classify the eggs O(n, 2n, q) in even characteristic that contain at least one sub pseudo-oval.

evidence.quote: 9. Classify the O(n, 2n, q)’s, q even, with at least one sub pseudo-oval.
For n = m such a set O(n, m, q) is called a pseudo-ovoid or a generalized ovoid or an [n − 1]-ovoid or an egg of PG(2n + m − 1, q); a [0]-ovoid of PG(3, q) is just an ovoid of PG(3, q).
For n = m such a set O(n, n, q) is called a pseudo-oval or a generalized oval or an [n − 1]-oval of PG(3n − 1, q).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the projective space PG(4n−1, q), where q is even. A set O(n, 2n, q) (an "egg") is a family of q^{2n}+1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(4n−1, q) such that any three of them span a (3n−1)-dimensional subspace, and such that for every element E of the family there exists a (3n−1)-dimensional subspace (the tangent space at E) containing E and meeting every other element of the family trivially. A sub pseudo-oval of such an egg is a subset of q^n+1 elements of O(n, 2n, q) all contained in a common (3n−1)-dimensional subspace of PG(4n−1, q) and forming a pseudo-oval there (i.e., a family of q^n+1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-spaces in PG(3n−1, q), any three of which span the whole space).

Problem: Classify, up to projective equivalence, all eggs O(n, 2n, q) in PG(4n−1, q) with q even that contain at least one sub pseudo-oval.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant partial results exist. Work on eggs in PG(4n−1, q), q even, containing a pseudo-conic or a pseudo-pointed conic (special types of sub pseudo-ovals) has shown such eggs are classical/elementary under additional hypotheses. However, a complete classification covering an arbitrary sub pseudo-oval remains, to the best of available evidence, not fully achieved.

status_evidence.title: Eggs in PG(4n−1,q), q even, containing a pseudo-pointed conic
status_evidence.snippet: An egg in PG(4n−1,q), q even, contains a pseudo-pointed conic ... if and only if the egg is elementary and the ovoid is either an elliptic quadric in PG(3,4) or a Tits ovoid in PG(3,8).
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification under the stronger hypothesis of containing a pseudo-pointed conic.

status_evidence.title: Eggs in PG(4n−1,q), q even, containing a pseudo-conic
status_evidence.snippet: The egg O(n,2n,q) of PG(4n−1,q), q even, is classical if and only if either O is good at some element and contains at least one pseudo-conic, or O contains at least two intersecting pseudo-conics.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification for the pseudo-conic case under additional hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Regular pseudo-hyperovals and regular pseudo-ovals in even characteristic
status_evidence.snippet: A pseudo-(hyper)oval in PG(3n-1,q), q even, n prime, with every element inducing a Desarguesian spread, is elementary.
status_evidence.claim: Related classification results for pseudo-ovals in even characteristic.
